chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh narrated from Abū Khadījah Sālim ibn Mukram al-Jammāl, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said:

Beware that some of you do not take others among you for judgment to the people of tyranny. Rather, look to a man from among you who knows something of our judgments, then appoint him among you, for I have indeed appointed him a judge; so seek judgment before him.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْجَوْرِ: the people of injustice and tyranny who exercise illegitimate judgment
key_terms.رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ: a man from among your own community
key_terms.فَتَحَاكَمُوا إِلَيْهِ: refer your disputes to him for judgment
key_terms.قَاضِيًا: a judge authorized to adjudicate disputes
key_terms.قَضَايَانَا: the judgments and legal rulings transmitted from the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.يَعْلَمُ شَيْئًا مِنْ قَضَايَانَا: one who knows something of our judicial rulings and legal judgments

ai.seo_question: Whom did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام permit the Shi'a to appoint as a judge in their disputes?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام forbids the believers from seeking judgment through unjust authorities. Instead, he directs them to appoint someone from among themselves who knows the rulings of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and to refer disputes to him. The hadith establishes a principle of legitimate religious adjudication within the community.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3216 - Ahmad ibn A'idh narrated from Abu Khadijah Salim ibn Mukram al-Jammal, who said:
Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Beware that none of you should take another to judgment before the people of tyranny. Instead, look for a man among you who knows something of our judgments, and appoint him as a judge between you, for indeed I have appointed him as a judge. So refer to him for judgment."
